"""Identifier case conversion."""

from __future__ import annotations


def snake_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert an identifier or phrase to ``snake_case``.

    Spaces, hyphens and underscores separate words. A change from a lowercase
    letter or digit to an uppercase one also starts a new word
    (``helloWorld`` -> ``hello_world``). A run of consecutive uppercase
    letters belongs to a single word (an acronym); only the final uppercase
    letter of such a run that is followed by a lowercase letter starts a new
    word (``HTTPServer`` -> ``http_server``, ``XMLHttpRequest`` ->
    ``xml_http_request``, ``userID`` -> ``user_id``). The result is lowercase,
    never contains two underscores in a row, and never starts or ends with one.

    Args:
        text: Input identifier, e.g. ``camelCase``, ``PascalCase`` or
            ``kebab-case``.

    Returns:
        The ``snake_case`` form of ``text``.
    """
    pieces: list[str] = []
    for index, char in enumerate(text):
        if char in " -_":
            if pieces and pieces[-1] != "_":
                pieces.append("_")
            continue
        if (
            char.isupper()
            and index > 0
            and pieces and pieces[-1] != "_"
            and (
                text[index - 1].islower()
                or text[index - 1].isdigit()
                or (
                    text[index - 1].isupper()
                    and index + 1 < len(text)
                    and text[index + 1].islower()
                )
            )
        ):
            pieces.append("_")
        pieces.append(char.lower())
    return "".join(pieces).strip("_")

"""Identifier case conversion."""

from __future__ import annotations


def snake_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert an identifier or phrase to ``snake_case``.

    Spaces, hyphens and underscores separate words. A change from a lowercase
    letter or digit to an uppercase one also starts a new word
    (``helloWorld`` -> ``hello_world``). A run of consecutive uppercase
    letters belongs to a single word (an acronym); only the final uppercase
    letter of such a run that is followed by a lowercase letter starts a new
    word (``HTTPServer`` -> ``http_server``, ``XMLHttpRequest`` ->
    ``xml_http_request``, ``userID`` -> ``user_id``). The result is lowercase,
    never contains two underscores in a row, and never starts or ends with one.

    Args:
        text: Input identifier, e.g. ``camelCase``, ``PascalCase`` or
            ``kebab-case``.

    Returns:
        The ``snake_case`` form of ``text``.
    """
    pieces: list[str] = []
    for index, char in enumerate(text):
        if char in " -_":
            if pieces and pieces[-1] != "_":
                pieces.append("_")
            continue
        if (
            char.isupper()
            and index > 0
            and pieces and pieces[-1] != "_"
            and (
                text[index - 1].islower()
                or text[index - 1].isdigit()
                or (
                    text[index - 1].isupper()
                    and index + 1 < len(text)
                    and text[index + 1].islower()
                )
            )
        ):
            pieces.append("_")
        pieces.append(char.lower())
    return "".join(pieces).strip("_")
